selected_problem: Fresh-main inspection and direct reproduction found that ChangesetStore optimistic-concurrency checks were content-addressed only. Replacing an existing file object with a different file containing identical bytes after staging preserved the same sha256, so apply accepted the replacement and overwrote it. The rollback side had the same sovereignty defect: replacing an applied file object with another object containing the same postimage bytes allowed rollback to overwrite the replacement.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The committed four-mode router selects DEEP_DEVELOPMENT through the singular evidence-rich bottleneck gate; no mode rotation was forced.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt is claimed. Selection/routing come from committed source-contract replay over fresh-main evidence while the hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained transiently unavailable.

pre_fix_reproduction.apply_same_content_replacement: EXPECTED FAILURE reproduced on canonical base: stage a.txt, atomically replace a.txt with a different file object containing the same preimage bytes, then apply; old code accepted it and overwrote the replacement.
pre_fix_reproduction.rollback_same_content_replacement: The same hash-only logic existed on rollback: a different replacement object with identical postimage bytes could satisfy rollback preflight and be overwritten.

changes: WorkspaceService.stat now reports a best-effort object identity derived from filesystem dev:ino when the platform exposes a non-zero inode value.
New changesets use protocol taowind-code.changeset.v0.3 and snapshot the preimage object identity alongside hash/size/content.
Apply preflight rejects an existing target whose object identity differs from the staged preimage even when bytes/hash are identical.
Apply receipts record post-apply object identity; rollback preflight uses that receipt to reject same-content replacement objects before the first restoration.

Compatibility is fail-soft for older changesets or platforms where identity is unavailable: identity comparison is enforced only when the stored expected identity is present; all existing hash, existence, type, ancestor and path boundaries remain active.
truth_boundaries: Filesystem object identity is best-effort and is only enforced when Node exposes a non-zero inode identity. This does not claim a portable cryptographic object identity across every filesystem/platform.
Ancestor directory inode replacement remains outside this focused target-object closure.
Filesystem crash-level atomicity for arbitrary I/O/process failure remains unresolved.
Validation workspace confinement remains a broader unresolved sovereignty boundary.
Arbitrary complex repository semantic synthesis remains UNRESOLVED.
No GitHub Actions were intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push was used, and no credential, payment, formal Release or destructive/irreversible external action was performed.
